parts.name: body loop

physics.Basic_description: The main D-shaped loop of the carabiner, appearing as a smooth, white-anodized aluminum tube with a consistent circular cross-section.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the primary structural strength and load-bearing capacity for attaching ropes or gear.
physics.Grasped_description: A parallel jaw gripper can securely grasp the spine or the curved bottom of the loop.
physics.reason: Carabiner bodies are typically forged or machined from solid metal stock to withstand high tensile loads, not hollow shells.

parts.description: The main D-shaped loop of the carabiner, appearing as a smooth, white-anodized aluminum tube with a consistent circular cross-section.
parts.function: Provides the primary structural strength and load-bearing capacity for attaching ropes or gear.

parts.name: nose slot

physics.Basic_description: A small green-colored segment at the top tip of the body loop, representing the nose where the gate closes.
physics.Functional_description: Contains the slot or notch that captures the gate nose to keep the carabiner closed.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and integrated into the tip to be a primary grasp target.
physics.reason: Part of the solid forged body structure.

parts.description: A small green-colored segment at the top tip of the body loop, representing the nose where the gate closes.
parts.function: Contains the slot or notch that captures the gate nose to keep the carabiner closed.

parts.name: gate bar

physics.Basic_description: The straight blue-colored bar that forms the movable gate, matching the material and finish of the main body.
physics.Functional_description: Swings open to allow attachment of items and closes to secure them within the loop.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped along its length to manipulate the gate, though usually the body is preferred for stability.
physics.reason: Gate bars are solid metal rods or extrusions to resist bending forces.

parts.description: The straight blue-colored bar that forms the movable gate, matching the material and finish of the main body.
parts.function: Swings open to allow attachment of items and closes to secure them within the loop.

parts.name: gate key

physics.Basic_description: A small yellow-colored segment at the tip of the gate bar, representing the key nose mechanism.
physics.Functional_description: Engages with the body nose slot to lock the gate in the closed position (keylock system).
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and precise to be grasped directly.
physics.reason: Integral part of the solid gate bar tip.

parts.description: A small yellow-colored segment at the tip of the gate bar, representing the key nose mechanism.
parts.function: Engages with the body nose slot to lock the gate in the closed position (keylock system).

parts.name: hinge pin

physics.Basic_description: A small orange-colored cylindrical pin located at the base of the gate, acting as the pivot point.
physics.Functional_description: Allows the gate to rotate open and closed relative to the body.
physics.Grasped_description: Not graspable; it is a small internal fastener/pivot point.
physics.reason: Pins are solid metal cylinders to handle shear forces.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained

simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)
